column1: # p189 — ACTION MY. Row-level CHURN of the 12-page recency census against p188's stored 240.
# Channel: github.com/topics/<t>?s=updated via WebFetch (P93's channel). 20 rows/page.
# THE INTERVAL IS NOT WHAT THE ACTION ASSUMED, AND THAT IS THE FIRST FINDING.
# ACTION MY was written to measure churn "48 hours on". Commit timestamps say otherwise:
#   p188  2026-10-14 03:19:21 Z   <- 70 minutes after p187, NOT one day
# p188's own evidence file says it re-read the pages "one day later" than p187. It did not.
# So the explanation p188 offered for the 11.5-point drop -- "the recency window may have
# moved in one day" -- was never available to it. 70 minutes cannot move 28 of 240 rows.
# CONTROLS (the standing rule: a probe returning one verdict for every row measured nothing)
#   5/5 and 2/2. TIGHT index this pass: 2 025 slugs (p188 measured 1 993).
#   CACHE CONTROL: WebFetch caches 15 min/URL and the interval is 28 min, so the reads are
#   live. Corroborated by the data: 4 of 12 pages DID change, so no page is cache-frozen.
# LIMB 1 needed churn >=25%. LIMB 2 needed churn <25%.
# LIMB 2 FIRES ON THE FACT: churn 14/239 = 5.9%, far under the 25% threshold. The page is
# STABLE over this interval. Eight of twelve pages changed by ZERO rows.
# LIMB 2'S STATED CONSEQUENCE IS REFUTED. It said: the page is stable, therefore the
# 11.5-point drop WAS a counting error. It was not. A THIRD mechanism, in neither limb,
# accounts for it, and it is measurable:
#   THE ABSENT RATE FALLS BECAUSE THIS KB INGESTS THE ROWS IT CENSUSES.
#   absent, all rows, TIGHT index:   p188 162/240 = 67.5%   p189 144/239 = 60.3%
#   -> a further 7.2-point fall in 28 minutes, with only 14 of 239 rows changed.
#   14 rows flipped ABSENT -> PRESENT. Every one is cited in a KB PAGE, not merely in an
#   verticals/solutions.md. p188 INGESTED them. The index grew 1 993 -> 2 025.
# ROWS THAT FLIPPED a->p IN 28 MINUTES, AND THE PAGE THAT NOW CITES THEM:
# CONSEQUENCE, AND IT RETIRES AN INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN A FIGURE:
# The "absent rate" was read for three passes as a measure of how much of the CHANNEL this
# KB has not yet seen. It is not. It is a lagging gauge of this KB's own INGEST BACKLOG,
# and it falls by ~6 points per pass BY CONSTRUCTION, as a consequence of the work being
# done. p187's 79%, p188's 67.5% and p189's 60.3% are not three estimates of one quantity
# in disagreement; they are one quantity declining because the backlog is being cleared.
# NOBODY OVER-COUNTED. 🟢 RULE: never quote the absent rate as channel coverage. Quote it
# as "rows not yet ingested", with its pass number, or do not quote it.
# WHAT DOES MEASURE THE CHANNEL: the NEW-SUPPLY rate. 12 unique slugs appeared across 12
# pages in 28 minutes; 10 of the 12 (83%) are absent from the KB. That is the sustainable
# intake number, and it is the one a plan can be built on.
